chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: The Calumet City club scene
summary: Calumet City was like 52nd Street, with steady white bands and weekend jobs for Black groups.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I want to ask you something about what you said about Calumet City. You said it was like 52nd Street. Tell me more about that. How do you mean? You said there were a lot of clubs, were other major musicians working in them, was it only a weekend situation?
No it was a weekend situation; but the ones that were steady were caucasians, you know. When they wanted a black ethnic group. it was weekend, like Saturday night, you know.
But there was music steadily there?
How close is Calumet City to Chicago?
Oh, about--let's see, you had to go through Gary--no, you didn't have to go through Gary, you had to go through Robbins, Illinois, to get there. I'd say about 15 or 20 miles.
So it probably drew some from Chicago, the audience.
